source_text: Adhibeo super haec ipsarum doctrinarum recognitionem quae tunc sub apostolis fuerunt ab isdem apostolis et demonstratae et deieratae. Nam et sic facilius traducentur, dum aut iam tunc fuisse deprehenduntur, aut ex illis quae iam tunc fuerunt seminia sumpsisse. Paulus in prima ad Corinthios notat negatores et dubitatores resurrectionis. Haec opinio propria Sadducaeorum. Partem eius usurpat Marcion et Apelles et Valentinus, et si qui alii resurrectionem carnis infringunt. Et ad Galatas scribens invehitur in observatores et defensores circumcisionis et legis. Hebionis haeresis sic est. Timotheum instruens nuptiarum quoque interdictores suggillat. Ita instituunt Marcion et Apelles, eius secutor. Aeque tangit eos qui dicerent factam iam resurrectionem. Id de se Valentiniani asseverant. Sed et cum genealogies indeterminatas nominat, Valentinus agnoscitur, apud quem Aeon ille nescio qui novi et non unius nominis generat ex sua Charite Sensum et Veritatem, et hi aeque procreant ex se Sermonem et Vitam, dehinc et isti generant Hominem et Ecclesiam, de qua prima ogdoade Aeonum exinde decem alii, et duodecim reliqui Aeones miris nominibus oriuntur in meram fabulam triginta Aeonum. Idem apostolus, cum improbat elementis servientes, aliquid Hermogenis ostendit, qui materiam non natam introducens deo non nato eam comparat, et ita matrem elementorum deam faciens potest ei servire quam deo comparat. Ioannes vero in Apocalypsi idolothyta edentes et stupra committentes iubetur castigare. Sunt et nunc alii Nicolaitae. Gaiana haeresis dicitur. At in epistula eos maxime antichristos vocat qui Christum negarent in carnem venisse, et qui non putarent Iesum esse filium dei. Illud Marcion, hoc Hebion vindicavit. Simonianae autem magiae disciplina angelis serviens utique et ipsa inter idololatrias deputabatur et a Petro apostolo in ipso Simone damnabatur.
thought_title: The apostles already marked and condemned the doctrines now held by heretics
orientation: Tertullian is showing that the doctrines of present-day heretics were already known and condemned by the apostles in their own time.
pass_a_gloss: I bring in, beyond these things, a review of the very doctrines which were then under the apostles, both demonstrated and condemned by those same apostles. For in this way they will be more easily refuted, while they are either caught as having existed already then, or as having taken seeds from those things which already existed then. Paul in the first letter to the Corinthians marks the deniers and doubters of the resurrection. This opinion is proper to the Sadducees. Marcion and Apelles and Valentinus usurp a part of it, and any others who weaken the resurrection of the flesh. And writing to the Galatians he inveighs against the observers and defenders of circumcision and the law. This is the heresy of Ebion. Instructing Timothy he also rebukes the forbidder of marriages. Thus Marcion and Apelles, his follower, teach. Equally he touches those who would say that the resurrection has already happened. The Valentinians assert this about themselves. But also when he names endless genealogies, Valentinus is recognized, in whom that Aeon, I know not who, of a new and not single name, generates from his own Charis Sense and Truth, and these equally procreate from themselves Word and Life, then these also generate Man and Church, from which first ogdoad of Aeons, then ten others, and twelve remaining Aeons with wonderful names arise into a mere fable of thirty Aeons. The same apostle, when he disapproves of those serving the elements, shows something of Hermogenes, who, introducing unbegotten matter, compares it to the unbegotten God, and thus making the mother of the elements a goddess, he can serve her whom he compares to God. John indeed in the Apocalypse is ordered to chastise those eating things sacrificed to idols and committing fornication. There are now also other Nicolaitans. It is called the Gaian heresy. But in the epistle he calls those especially antichrists who would deny that Christ has come in the flesh, and who would not think that Jesus is the son of God. Marcion vindicated the former, Ebion the latter. But the discipline of Simonian magic, serving angels, was certainly itself also counted among idolatries and was condemned by the apostle Peter in Simon himself.

choices.why: The verb deiero means to swear or declare under oath; in context it means the apostles formally condemned these doctrines, so 'condemned' captures the force without adding 'under oath' which would be awkward.
Traduco here means to expose or bring to shame; 'refuted' fits the argumentative context of showing heretics to be derivative.
The metaphor of seeds is important to Tertullian's argument that heresies grew from earlier errors; keeping 'seeds' preserves the image.
The verb means to attack verbally; 'inveighs against' captures the forceful rhetorical attack Paul makes.
Suggillo means to strike or bruise, metaphorically to reproach; 'rebukes' is the standard English for a corrective verbal blow.
Mera means pure or unmixed; 'mere fable' captures the dismissive tone toward the Valentinian system.

pass_b_english: I add to this a review of the very doctrines that existed under the apostles, which were both demonstrated and condemned by those same apostles. For in this way they will be more easily refuted, since they are either caught as having existed already then, or as having taken seeds from those things that already existed then.

Paul notes in his first letter to the Corinthians those who deny and doubt the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:12). This opinion belonged to the Sadducees. Marcion, Apelles, and Valentinus seize a part of it, and any others who weaken the resurrection of the flesh.
And writing to the Galatians, he inveighs against those who observe and defend circumcision and the law (Galatians 5:2-4). This is the heresy of Ebion.
Instructing Timothy, he also rebukes those who forbid marriage (1 Timothy 4:3). Marcion and Apelles, his follower, teach this.
He likewise touches those who said the resurrection had already happened (2 Timothy 2:18). The Valentinians assert this about themselves.

But when he names endless genealogies (1 Timothy 1:4), Valentinus is recognized. Among his followers, that Aeon—some new one with more than one name—generates from his own Grace, Sense and Truth; and these in turn produce from themselves Word and Life; and then these generate Man and Church, from which first group of eight Aeons ten others arise, and then the remaining twelve Aeons with astonishing names, into a mere fable of thirty Aeons.

The same apostle, when he disapproves of those serving the elements (Colossians 2:20), points to something of Hermogenes, who introduces uncreated matter and compares it to the uncreated God, and so makes the mother of the elements a goddess and can serve her whom he compares to God.
John, in the Revelation, is ordered to chastise those eating things sacrificed to idols and committing fornication (Revelation 2:14). There are now other Nicolaitans. It is called the Gaian heresy.

But in his epistle he calls those especially antichrists who deny that Christ has come in the flesh, and who do not think Jesus is the Son of God (1 John 4:3). Marcion claimed the former, Ebion the latter.
The discipline of Simonian magic, serving angels, was itself also counted among idolatries and was condemned by the apostle Peter in the person of Simon himself.

last_rejected.source_quote: Sed et cum genealogies indeterminatas nominat, Valentinus agnoscitur, ...
last_rejected.why: The Latin passage gives no scriptural reference; 1 Tim 1:4 does not discuss genealogies, so the citation is unwarranted.
last_rejected.fix: But when he names endless genealogies, Valentinus is recognized—...
last_rejected.ruling: 1 Tim 1:4 does mention 'genealogias' in Vulgate; translator's parenthetical scripture reference is accurate, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: The same apostle, when he disapproves of those serving the elements (Colossians 2:8), points to something of Hermogenes, who introduces uncreated matter and compares it to the uncreated God, and so makes the mother of the elements a goddess and can serve her whom he compares to God.

last_rejected.why: The source does not cite Colossians 2:8; that verse concerns philosophy, not "serving the elements," making the reference incorrect.

last_rejected.ruling: Col 2:8 Vulgate includes 'elementa mundi' and 'philosophia'; 'serving the elements' fits Col 2:8/2:20 context. Reference is defensible.

problems.why: Colossians 2:8 warns against philosophy and human tradition; 'serving the elements' is from Colossians 2:20 or Galatians 4:3.
